newsitem.title: USA: Foster Wheeler has pact to sell Glitsch.
newsitem.headline: Foster Wheeler has pact to sell Glitsch.

text.p: Foster Wheeler Corp said on Monday that it had signed a definitive agreement to sell substantially all of the business of its Glitsch International Inc subsidiary to Koch Engineering Co.
The cash sale, which Foster Wheeler expects to net about $250 million, is subject to governmental approvals and is expected to close in mid-summer, Foster Wheeler said in a statement.
Koch Engineering is a subsidiary of Koch Industries Inc, the second-largest privately held company in the United States, Foster Wheeler said.
Glitsch is a supplier of mass transfer systems and a designer and manufacturer of chemical separations equipment. In 1996 Glitsch revenues were about $300 million, Foster Wheeler said.

"The sale will enhance our financial flexibility and allow us to reinvest in higher growth opportunities within our core engineering and construction, energy equipment and power systems business groups," said Richard Swift, president and chief executive of Foster Wheeler.
Foster Wheeler Corp offers a range of design, engineering, construction and manufacturing services.
